response.query: What precise regularity, mixing, and contraction conditions suffice to prove a mean-field limit and propagation-of-chaos for decentralized two-armed Thompson Sampling under partial observability?
response.answer: For decentralized two-armed Thompson Sampling under partial observability, mean-field limit and propagation-of-chaos require independent initial conditions and weak interactions. Uniform convergence and Lipschitz continuity conditions are essential.

results.title: Mean-field description and propagation of chaos in networks of Hodgkin-Huxley and FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons | The Journal of Mathematical Neuroscience | Springer Nature Link
results.content: # Mean-field description and propagation of chaos in networks of Hodgkin-Huxley and FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons. We derive the mean-field equations arising as the limit of a network of interacting spiking neurons, as the number of neurons goes to infinity. The neurons belong to a fixed number of populations and are represented either by the Hodgkin-Huxley model or by one of its simplified version, the FitzHugh-Nagumo model. Under the condition that all neurons’ initial conditions are drawn independently from the same law that depends only on the population they belong to, we prove that a propagation of chaos phenomenon takes place, namely that in the mean-field limit, any finite number of neurons become independent and, within each population, have the same probability distribution. We also show the results of some numerical experiments that indicate that the mean-field equations are a good representation of the mean activity of a finite size network, even for modest sizes.

results.title: #11481 - Propagation of chaos in mean field networks of FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons
results.content: ## Laetitia Colombani ; Pierre Le Bris - Propagation of chaos in mean field networks of FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons. **Propagation of chaos in mean field networks of FitzHugh-Nagumo neurons**Article. We assume that the neurons follow the stochastic FitzHugh-Nagumo model, whose specificity is the non-linearity with a cubic term. We prove a result of uniform in time propagation of chaos of this model in a mean-field framework. We simultaneously construct a solution of the $N$-particle system and $N$ independent copies of the non-linear McKean-Vlasov limit in such a way that, considering an appropriate semi-metric that takes into account the various possible behaviors of the processes, the two solutions tend to get closer together as $N$ increases, uniformly in time. The reflection coupling allows us to deal with the non-convexity of the underlying potential in the dynamics of the quantities defining our network, and show independence at the limit for the system in mean field interaction with sufficiently small Lipschitz continuous interactions.
